story_type: rocket ignition seen from cameras on the launch deck
hook: These cameras sat right beside a Moon rocket's engines at ignition.
narration: These cameras sat on the launch deck, right beside a Moon rocket's engines.
This was Artemis I, at one forty-seven in the morning on November sixteenth, 2022, at Kennedy Space Center.
The sparks come first. They burn off stray hydrogen gas around the engines before ignition.
Then water floods the deck to soak up the heat and the sound.
The four main engines lit, glowing under the core stage.
[short pause] Last came the two solid rocket boosters, and the whole view turned to fire.
Together, they made more than eight point eight million pounds of thrust.
outcome: Artemis I launched, and Orion splashed down in the Pacific twenty-five and a half days later, after a trip to the Moon.
title: Moon rocket ignition from the launch deck
description:
Engineering cameras on the mobile launcher deck at Launch Pad 39B watched the SLS rocket's engines and boosters ignite as Artemis I lifted off from Kennedy Space Center on Nov. 16, 2022.

At 12:40 p.m. EST, Dec. 11, 2022, NASA’s Orion spacecraft for the Artemis I mission splashed down in the Pacific Ocean after a 25.5 day mission to the Moon.

NASA’s Space Launch System (SLS) rocket with the Orion spacecraft atop launches the agency’s Artemis I flight test, Wednesday, Nov. 16 from Launch Complex 39B at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. The Moon rocket and spacecraft lifted off at 1:47 a.m. ET.
